title: Slowquest: Quest 1: The Goblin Guard - Review and Let's Read
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DohrPYUe11o

This is where the Dungeon Dive begins. Daniel (@dungeondive) calls it "a really simple video for the first video for this channel": a read-through of Slowquest: Quest 1, The Goblin Guard, a tiny handmade pick-your-path booklet written and illustrated by Bodie Hartley. He places it in two revivals. One is the cheap, artisanal descendants of the Choose Your Own Adventure books he grew up on in the 70s and 80s. The other is the far heavier gamebooks like Fabled Lands and DestinyQuest, which he promises to cover later.

He is candid about the price. Shipped from Australia, each booklet costs about ten dollars and takes minutes to finish. He still thinks it's worth paying for something visibly handmade, and he admires the clean, stippled, Moebius-like art and the opening promise of "finite possibilities."

He plays two paths. Charging the door like a barbarian ends with a goblin's foot, a pit, a closed hatch and a lonely death wondering whether anyone will remember you. Approaching quietly leads to a conversation with Glub Dub, an extortionate goblin who is easily distracted by a question about his mother, and then to a treasure worth less than the map you bought to find the dungeon. Daniel closes by asking viewers for more DIY gamebooks.

----

This is the channel's very first video: a ten-minute handmade booklet and a goblin named Glub Dub. What small, handmade game or gamebook has stuck with you more than a big-box release?
